title: Mean baseline
hypothesis: Predicting the training mean of log-price scores worst; every real model must beat it.
rationale: Provides the zero-skill reference so improvements can be expressed as relative gains.
implementation: models.build_mean_baseline: DummyRegressor(strategy='mean'); features: base.
evaluation: KFold(5, shuffle, seed 42) on log1p(SalePrice); metric RMSE on log scale; preprocessing refit per fold
interpretation: RMSE 0.3987: this is roughly the standard deviation of log-price, the floor any model must beat. Anything near it has learned nothing.

title: OLS on numeric columns
hypothesis: Plain least squares on numeric columns already removes most of the error.
rationale: Cheapest informative model; isolates what numeric features alone provide, before categories or regularisation.
implementation: models.build_ols_numeric: NumericMedianImputer (training-fold median) + LinearRegression; Id dropped.
evaluation: KFold(5, shuffle, seed 42) on log1p(SalePrice); metric RMSE on log scale; preprocessing refit per fold
interpretation: RMSE 0.1599 (std 0.0348), 60% below the mean baseline. Numeric columns alone carry most of the signal; unregularised OLS on correlated areas is the benchmark regularisation must beat. A large fold std would flag instability from collinearity.

title: Ridge alpha=10, one-hot
hypothesis: Adding one-hot categories with L2 shrinkage beats numeric-only OLS.
rationale: Houses are strongly driven by Neighborhood and quality; shrinkage tames the 200+ one-hot columns.
implementation: models.build_ridge(alpha=10): LazyPreprocessor (neighborhood-median LotFrontage, median, RobustScaler, one-hot) + Ridge.
evaluation: KFold(5, shuffle, seed 42) on log1p(SalePrice); metric RMSE on log scale; preprocessing refit per fold
interpretation: RMSE 0.1409 (std 0.0316). First model using categorical variables via one-hot and shrinkage; compare with OLS-numeric to see what categories plus regularisation add. alpha=10 is an untuned guess; the grid in run_linear_family.py refines it.

title: XGBoost defaults
hypothesis: An untuned gradient-boosted tree model is competitive with regularised linear models on this data.
rationale: Trees capture interactions and non-linearity automatically; the default run shows how much tuning must still add.
implementation: models.build_xgboost(): XGBRegressor library defaults (seed 42, 8 threads) on one-hot unscaled inputs.
evaluation: KFold(5, shuffle, seed 42) on log1p(SalePrice); metric RMSE on log scale; preprocessing refit per fold
interpretation: RMSE 0.1487 (std 0.0190) with library defaults. Gives the untuned booster level; tuning (B3) and outlier policy (B2) are judged against it.

title: Ablation: base / elasticnet
hypothesis: Reference configuration.
rationale: Ablation isolates each engineered group's contribution under identical folds and models.
implementation: features.FEATURE_SETS groups ['base']; preprocessing: default preprocessing; model houseprices.models:build_elasticnet {'alpha': 0.001, 'l1_ratio': 0.5}
evaluation: KFold(5, shuffle, seed 42) on log1p(SalePrice); metric RMSE on log scale; preprocessing refit per fold
interpretation: Reference run for elasticnet: RMSE 0.1379 (std 0.0353). All deltas for this model are measured against it.

title: Outlier policy drop_candidate_outliers | Ridge | all features
hypothesis: Training-fold-only row policy 'drop_candidate_outliers' changes the CV RMSE of Ridge (alpha=10, skew_log1p) relative to keeping every row. Auditor note Q4: drop_GrLivArea_gt_4000 also removes Ids 692 and 1183 (legitimate expensive houses) besides the two EDA candidates 524 and 1299, so it is a distinct policy, not a proxy for the Id list.
rationale: Two extreme-area, low-price houses (Ids 524, 1299) can pull linear fits; trees are expected to be less sensitive. The GrLivArea>4000 rule is evaluated separately because it also drops legitimate expensive houses (Ids 692, 1183). Auditor note Q4: drop_GrLivArea_gt_4000 also removes Ids 692 and 1183 (legitimate expensive houses) besides the two EDA candidates 524 and 1299, so it is a distinct policy, not a proxy for the Id list.
implementation: houseprices.models:build_ridge({'alpha': 10.0, 'preprocessor_kwargs': {'skew_log1p': True}}); feature_set=base+areas+baths+ages+quality_interactions+ordinal_quality; train_row_filter=drop_candidate_outliers applied after the split to training rows only; validation fold untouched.
evaluation: KFold(5, shuffle, seed 42) on log1p(SalePrice); metric RMSE on log scale; preprocessing refit per fold
interpretation: RMSE 0.1348 (fold std 0.0345). Versus keep_all: paired fold difference +0.0044 (SE 0.0053), worse (higher); the difference does not exceed one paired standard error. Worse than the best policy (keep_all, 0.1304) by +0.0044 (paired SE 0.0053); within noise of the best, so not rejected.
notes: Paired differences use identical folds (KFold 5, seed 42). Means across policies: keep_all=0.1304, drop_candidate_outliers=0.1348, drop_GrLivArea_gt_4000=0.1360
